liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Distorto (Crazy Fingers) Jam** (2 reviews): The Distorto treatment of Crazy Fingers is described as very cool and worth repeated listening; Gives the Crazy Fingers theme a heavy, metal-like approach [5][6]
- **Stronger Than Dirt Jam** (1 review, 1 other source): A Stronger Than Dirt jam runs about two minutes, then moves into drum noodling and talk before returning to the jam; Reviewer believes the jams labeled Stronger Than Dirt are actually King Solomon's jams [1][9]
- **Spacey Noodling Jam** (2 reviews): On track 9, Jerry fiddles with Tico Tico; once learned, Jerry, Bob, Keith and Billy play it from 6:15 to 9:00; Track 9 has the band working through Tico Tico, with Jerry also playing a bit of Nature Boy [8][11]
- **The Music Never Stopped Jam** (2 reviews): The Music Never Stopped takes are singled out as showing how the band's rehearsal work paid off; With each successive take the song tightens, and licks that would last for years emerge [3][5]
- **Bouncey Jam** (1 review): Slow to start, but once it gets going it turns into a hypnotic Dead groove [11]
- **They Love Each Other Jam** (1 other source): A jam resembling They Love Each Other slides into a slow jam that sounds like Not Fade Away, then noodling [1]
- **Jungle Music Jam** (1 review): The band riffs on two Meters tunes from the 1974 album Rejuvenation: Just Kissed My Baby and Hey Pockey Way [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **Distorto (Crazy Fingers) Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Distorto (Crazy Fingers) Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Bouncey Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Studio Talk**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Stronger Than Dirt Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Stronger Than Dirt Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]
- **Studio Talk**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Girl From Ipanema Jam**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1975-02-28.sbd.smith.93779.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 133 min; rated 4.27/5 by 15 [1]

## Around the show

- Someone asks for a take to be played back, and a musician asks Dan to raise the snare in his monitor [1]
- The band was evidently listening to the Meters' 1974 album Rejuvenation around this time [4]
- Reviewer says the session shows a thoroughly rehearsed band, contradicting Garcia's remark that rehearsals were perfunctory [3]
- Described as the first 1975 rehearsal available, featuring several jams that were soon dropped [6]
- The Distorto is the same one used as a bonus track on the Blues for Allah disc [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1975-02-28.sbd.smith.93779.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Dan Healy; transferred by Matt Smith; source: SBD > MR (Vault Reel) [1]. Also: This material was aired on KBOO radio some time ago, according to the reviewer [2]
